business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Commodity Trade in Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Continental Law; French-inspired commercial and administrative doctrine; unitary national legal system with no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: BLEU (Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union) network of 100+ active bilateral investment treaties

Luxembourg double taxation agreement network (80+ active DTAs), including treaties with major dairy-export counterparties (e.g., China-Luxembourg DTA signed 28 March 2019; DTAs with Germany, France, Netherlands, UAE, Singapore, Switzerland)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; ratification suspended but MFN/GATT disciplines apply)
WTO Agreement on Agriculture and GATT 1994 (tariff schedules for HS 0402 whole/skimmed milk powder)
EU-Japan Economic Partnership Agreement and EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (dairy tariff-rate quotas and sanitary disciplines)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: CSSF-supervised AML/CFT framework: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing (as amended, consolidated version); CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 (as amended by CSSF Regulation No 20-05); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (Loi RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020 on digitalisation; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 August 2019 on RBE functioning; Articles 506-1 to 506-6 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code; Law of 19 December 2020 on the freezing and confiscation of criminal assets implementing UN/EU restrictive measures; EU AMLD4 and AMLD5 (Directives (EU) 2015/849 and 2018/843) transposed thereunder.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport of each ultimate beneficial owner (individual UBO exceeding 25% direct/indirect interest)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or certified legal officer in the UBO country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (Apostille Convention 1961) OR consular legalization at a Luxembourg embassy/consulate for non-Hague-jurisdiction documents

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address of each UBO (utility bill or bank statement dated within three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or licensed bank of the UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization; notarized French/German/English translation required if original is non-Latin script

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing of any corporate general partner (gérant) and any corporate limited partner above the 25% UBO threshold
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent trade/company registry in the corporate partner's country of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR consular legalization (apostilled registry extract; translation certified where required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter (banker's reference) on bank letterhead for each founding partner, including SWIFT-contact verification
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relation bank of the founding partner (licensed credit institution)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled signature page OR consular legalization; SWIFT/KYC contact verification by the Luxembourg bank

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Curriculum vitae and professional standing certificate of the designated local gérant (manager) evidencing commercial substance
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Previous employer, professional body, or registered-agent firm of the manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized copy with Hague Apostille where the manager is a foreign resident; otherwise notarized Luxembourg statement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of UBOs, general partners, and manager against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (FIU Luxembourg), UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and Luxembourg domestic restrictive-measures list; PEP determination under FATF Recommendation 12 and Article 3(7°) of the Law of 12 November 2004; enhanced due diligence triggered by PEP status, state-owned counterparty exposure, or high-risk third-country sourcing; continuous negative-media and sanctions re-screening required throughout the banking relationship per CSSF Regulation 12-02 Chapter 4 and CSSF AML/CFT circulars.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), electronic filing via eJustice.lu and LBR one-stop-shop
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Official filing language is French; the corporate name may be in French, German, Luxembourgish, or another living language using Latin script; any non-Latin script (e.g., Cyrillic, Chinese) requires a statutory transliteration into Latin characters in the limited partnership agreement; the name must not be identical to an existing RCS entry, must not be misleading, must not prejudice public order, and must include the legal-form designation 'SCSp' or 'Société en commandite spéciale'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Fonds / OPC / SICAV / SICAR / FIS (financial-sector instruments)
Luxembourg / Luxemburg (misleading sovereign or national link)
Croix-Rouge / Kommanditär (protected international or institutional designations)
Any EU protected designation of origin (PDO) or geographical indication (PGI) term transferred onto the corporate name without authorization
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon RCS name refusal, the applicant may (i) refile the incorporation docket with a modified name within 30 days without losing priority; (ii) file an appeal against the Registrar's decision before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement (Luxembourg or Diekirch) within 15 days of written notification, by application (requête) submitted through a Luxembourg avocat; (iii) where the refusal is purely linguistic, submit a certified translation and resume the pre-filing name check; no parallel filing of the identical rejected name is admissible pending the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or pure domiciliation address is legally permissible for an SCSp and satisfies the statutory registered-office requirement (Article 33-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915), provided the address is in Luxembourg and designated in the limited partnership agreement. However, for ISIC 4633 cross-border dairy commodity trading with SWIFT LC and TT wire payment rails, banks and customs/tax authorities (Administration des douanes et accises; ALVA) expect substantive local substance: a local gérant or general partner, Luxembourg bookkeeping, a local bank account, board/director decisions, and physical or contractual storage evidence for EU zero-rated intra-community supplies. Pure virtual-office structuring will be classified as substance-light and materially increases AML/EDD scrutiny and permanent-establishment litigation risk.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified at 12-18% per fiscal year for the trading-profile SCSp: ALVA (food-safety) and the customs administration perform documentary and on-site checks on dairy import/export operators; VAT intra-community supply audits of milk powder trigger periodic on-site verification of transport contracts, CMR consignment notes, and storage capacity. Unannounced inspections are more likely if the company claims zero-rating without physical handling evidence.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended by the Law of 23 June 2016 on the modernization of the Société en Commandite Spéciale (Articles 125-1 to 125-21), together with the Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (contrat de société) executed by private deed or notarial act, followed by mandatory RCS registration
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital for an SCSp; the partnership agreement determines the subscribed capital and payment schedule. A minimum initial contribution of EUR 12,500 is commercially recommended to demonstrate creditworthiness, although the law imposes no mandatory paid-up capital or escrow requirement.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA BOARD RESOLUTION (SCSp governance equivalent): RESOLVED, by the founding general partner and limited partners of LU SCSp: (1) the executed partnership agreement is approved and the SCSp is constituted under Luxembourg law; (2) the registered office is fixed at [Registered Address], Luxembourg; (3) [General Partner] is appointed sole manager, with full authority to subscribe capital, open bank accounts, and represent the partnership before public authorities; (4) the manager is authorised to apply for RCS registration, establishment permit, VAT and social security enrolment, and all regulatory filings; (5) all lawful acts performed during formation are ratified; (6) this resolution remains in force until revoked.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Execute Partnership Agreement (contrat de société)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary or private signature (acte sous seing privé); notarization is required only if real estate is contributed
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the SCSp articles of association including legal form, corporate name, registered office, corporate object, duration, identity of the general partner and limited partner, capital subscription and payment terms, management powers, and profit-sharing. Execute the deed by private signature or before a notary. Procure certified copies and banking references for subsequent filings.
required_dossiers: Valid passport or ID of each founding partner
Proof of registered office address (lease or deed)
Certificate of non-conviction for the general partner
Statement of capital subscription and payment terms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the deed is challenged, amend and re-execute the agreement; notarization cures formal defects in private deeds.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Registration to Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, online portal: www.lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the standard RCS application on the LBR portal and attach the executed partnership deed, registered office proof, and manager identification. Pay the administrative filing fee and submit the dossier for legal review. Upon approval, obtain the RCS registration number and the pending publication status.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement (notarized or private certified copy)
RCS application form signed by the manager
Power of attorney if filing through an agent
Identity documents and criminal record certificate of the manager
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Within 15 days of a query, correct or complete the registration dossier; request further guidance through the LBR helpdesk or corporate counsel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Verify Publication in RESA Electronic Gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Official Electronic Compilation of Companies and Associations (RESA), published by the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Monitor the RESA publication excerpt generated after RCS registration. Confirm that the legal information, including name, registered office, manager, and corporate object, matches the submitted deed. Retrieve the publication certificate for banking and counterparty due diligence.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Apply for correction through the LBR if the RESA extract differs from the deed; identified errors are cured against third parties upon corrected publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for SMEs (guichet.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the establishment permit application for wholesale trade in dairy products (ISIC 4633) through guichet.lu. Attach the RCS extract, manager's criminal record, and evidence of professional competence or prior business management experience. This permit is a precondition to legally carrying on commercial activities in Luxembourg.
required_dossiers: Manager identity and criminal record certificate
Proof of professional qualification or management experience
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file an administrative appeal with the Ministry of the Economy within 40 days; if incomplete, supplement the dossier and resubmit for further processing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Beneficial Ownership Register
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the ultimate beneficial owners of the SCSp in the national beneficial ownership register. Identify all natural persons owning or controlling more than 25% of the partnership. Maintain the information on a current basis and ensure access-restricted treatment unless a legitimate interest is demonstrated.
required_dossiers: Passport copies of ultimate beneficial owners
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Update the RBE filing upon any change; respond to LBR requests for evidence of UBO identification within the statutory deadline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for VAT and Social Security
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement (VAT) and Luxembourg Centre for Social Security (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete VAT registration through guichet.lu to obtain a Luxembourg VAT number; for EU cross-border trade in milk powder, confirm intra-EU reverse-charge or zero-rated supply treatment. Register directors or employees with CCSS for social insurance. For an SCSp with no employees, register as the paying entity for management indemnities and any profit distribution obligations.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If VAT or CCSS registration is queried, submit supplementary KYC or corporate documentation through guichet.lu and liaise with fiscal counsel to cure any deficiencies.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Corporate Bank Account and Ratify Pre-Formation Acts
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the SCSp's corporate bank account using the RCS certificate, partnership deed, establishment permit, and UBO identities. The manager shall present the final corporate governance checklist to the partners and execute the ratification resolution.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If account opening is delayed, supplement source-of-funds evidence or apply to an alternative institution; request a formal KYC decision letter to identify and remedy missing items.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy, Directorate General for SMEs (Autorisation d'Établissement)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Establishment Permit for Wholesale Trade of Whole and Skimmed Milk Powder (Class 4633 / NAICS 424430)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Protection Agency of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – Category C (no production or industrial installation; no mandatory EIA required for wholesale trading activities)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No on-site discharge or VOC emission thresholds apply. The SCSp must comply with municipal waste collection rules, packaging waste take-back obligations under the Law of 21 March 2017 on waste, and, if storing dairy products, Regulation (EC) 853/2004 food safety cold-chain requirements where applicable.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate for the registered office; structural load declaration for leased premises; occupational health and safety clearance under the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines, ITM) for office and any ancillary warehouse activity.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) - Luxembourg indirect tax (VAT) authority; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) - direct tax authority. Official portals: Guichet.lu (administrative portal), MyGuichet.lu (electronic filing and VAT e-services), and Luxembourg Business Registers (lbr.lu) for RNE/RCS registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: 1) Pre-requisite licences: obtain the commercial establishment authorisation under the Law of 2 September 2011 (autorisation d'établissement) and any food-sector registration with the Luxembourg Food Safety Administration (ALVA) for dairy product import/trading. 2) RNE registration: file the SCSp partnership agreement (no minimum capital) with the Luxembourg Business Registers and obtain the national business matricule number. 3) VAT registration: submit electronic form 640 (demande d'immatriculation a la TVA) to the AED via MyGuichet.lu using LuxTrust credentials; a VAT representative (représentant responsable) under Article 63 of the VAT Law must be appointed if the entity has no EU establishment. The SCSp, though lacking legal personality, is accepted as a distinct taxable person for VAT and obtains a VAT number in the format LU followed by 8 digits. 4) Direct tax: RNE registration automatically effects ACD identification; partners' tax residency and transparency statements are lodged as required. 5) E-filing activation: activate MyGuichet/eCDF for periodic VAT returns and EU recapitulative statements. Standard turnaround is 2 to 6 weeks from a complete application.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Luxembourg check-the-box exists for direct tax; the SCSp is fiscally transparent by default (Articles 175 to 184 LIR), with each partner taxed on its allocable share. Relevant elections and statutory triggers: (i) voluntary VAT identification below the EUR 35,000 small-business exemption (Article 57(2) VAT Law); (ii) Luxembourg VAT grouping election (assujetti unique, Article 60 VAT Law); (iii) US federal check-the-box election (IRC Section 7701, Form 8832) choosing corporate or transparent status for US participants, which may create hybrid outcomes; (iv) ATAD 2 reverse-hybrid reclassification (Law of 27 December 2019, as amended, effective 1 January 2022) whereby the SCSp may become subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax where participants' jurisdictions treat it as opaque; (v) hybrid mismatch disallowance and neutralisation rules applying to deductible payments under the same law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutee) under the Luxembourg VAT Law (loi du 12 fevrier 1979, modifiee), aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 in annual taxable turnover for the small-business exemption (Article 57 VAT Law); mandatory VAT identification once turnover exceeds EUR 35,000, upon intra-EU acquisitions exceeding EUR 10,000, or immediately when zero-rated exports are carried out and input VAT recovery is sought. Voluntary registration below the threshold is available.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg applies no real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, or digital stamping by the AED. The 2023 e-invoicing reform (Law of 3 August 2023) mandates PEPPOL-based structured e-invoicing under EN 16931: receiving capability from 1 January 2026 and issuance for domestic Luxembourg B2B transactions from 1 January 2027; cross-border EU issuance will follow the ViDA timeline (2030/2035). Invoices must satisfy Article 42-44 VAT Law content requirements, serialisation is not state-controlled, and e-invoices are exchanged via PEPPOL access points without prior tax authority approval.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of whole and skimmed milk powder to non-EU destinations qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 59 of the VAT Law, transposing Article 146 of Directive 2006/112/EC, provided the goods are dispatched to a destination outside the EU by the supplier or for its account and the export is evidenced by an EX-A customs declaration and proof of physical exit from the EU customs territory. Intra-EU supplies to VAT-identified customers are exempt under the same framework subject to a valid customer VAT number and filing of the recapitulative statement (ESL). Related freight, loading, packing and export-handling services directly linked to the exported goods are also zero-rated; B2B services to non-EU principals fall outside Luxembourg VAT under Articles 57-58 place-of-supply rules. The SCSp must hold contemporaneous evidence of zero-rating before filing the VAT return, and must separately substantiate input VAT recovery on purchasing, warehousing and logistics costs.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: EU Single Administrative Document (SAD) export declaration (EX-A) lodged at the competent customs office of export, with endorsement/control result confirming dispatch from EU customs territory

Bill of Lading (or CMR consignment note or IATA airway bill) evidencing physical exit of the milk powder consignment from the EU, matched to the commercial invoice, packing list and export declaration
Inward remittance certificate or SWIFT MT103 evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the non-EU buyer, supporting the 180-day repatriation benchmark
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AED may audit export zero-rating claims for up to 3 years after the chargeable period, extended to 5 years in fraud or serious irregularity cases. Unsubstantiated zero-rating results in retrospective VAT assessment at 16% plus statutory late-payment interest. Negligent or fraudulent claims attract fines under Articles 65-67 of the VAT Law and criminal referral (imprisonment up to 5 years and fines up to EUR 50,000), while invoicing and declaration breaches are fined under Article 61 of the VAT Law (from EUR 750 to EUR 25,000 per infraction). Following the 25 July 2021 anti-fraud reform, Article 68 of the VAT Law imposes joint and several VAT liability on any trader in the chain who knew or ought to have known of the fraud, and permits the AED to collect unpaid VAT directly from the contractual partner. Luxembourg imposes no statutory exchange-control repatriation deadline; the 180-day period reflects customary letter-of-credit and commodity contract terms and prudential tax documentation expectations.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) — Central Bank of Luxembourg; the CSSF (Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier) acts as the competent banking and AML supervisor for Luxembourg credit institutions
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a euro-area member state; the euro (EUR) is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account purposes. Free movement of capital is guaranteed under Article 63 TFEU, and there is no exchange-control or prior-authorisation regime for non-resident partners. Profit remittance and dividend or distribution payments from a pass-through SCSp are unrestricted, subject only to standard AML/KYC verification and CSSF reporting duties; no convertibility certificates or central-bank approvals are required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory export-proceeds surrender timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no BCL collection account requirement. Euro-denominated and foreign-currency export proceeds may be freely retained, repatriated, or offset against trade payables; only statistical balance-of-payments declarations to the BCL may apply above prescribed reporting thresholds.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account / Commodity Trade Finance Facility

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium (bridge-only). A Luxembourg-licensed or EU/EEA passporting electronic money institution (EMI) under PSD2 can hold a corporate account for an SCSp and route EUR traffic via TARGET2/SEPA, but such institutions generally do not provide documentary-letter-of-credit or commodity-trade settlement capabilities and impose custody limits on client funds. Unregulated or offshore non-EEA digital EMIs are not legally viable for Luxembourg corporate cash management: they do not comply with the Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering as amended, cannot be counterparties for a Luxembourg bank's internal policy, and would trigger CSSF-regulated bank KYC rejection. A full-service regulated credit institution is required before the commodity trading pipeline becomes operational.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Luxembourg law does not statutorily mandate a physical interview; under CSSF AML/CFT guidance identity verification may in principle be completed via secure video identification. In practice, however, Tier 1 Luxembourg banks require the general partner (GP), the founder's representative, and each beneficial owner to attend at least one in-person onboarding interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises or at a Luxembourg notary/consulate for identity certification; remote-only account opening is granted only to low-risk existing institutional clients and is rarely extended to newly formed SCSp commodity trading vehicles. A physical board or partner KYC session in Luxembourg City is therefore the prudent baseline on-boarding procedure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO identification and RBE register consistency
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised limited partnership agreement (LPA); current extract from the Luxembourg Register of Commercial and Companies (RCS); certificate of registration in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); passport copies and proof of address of each natural-person UBO holding 25%+; beneficial-ownership declaration signed by the general partner

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-transparent SCSp structure treated as suspicious pass-through
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent Luxembourg tax opinion confirming pass-through status and absence of tax-evasion purpose; CRS/FATCA registration confirmations; documentation of commercial substance (registered office, local corporate secretary, bank mandate, risk-management function); explanatory statement of the investor chain

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds and source of wealth for initial capital injection
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: 12-month bank statements of contributing partner entities; notarised share register and ownership chain; audited financial statements or certified management accounts of the ultimate parent; executed subscription and capital-call documentation; evidence of dividend or sale consideration underlying partner wealth

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trading red flags (ISIC 4633 milk powder) — sanctions, dual-use, or fraud
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master trade agreements, purchase orders and invoices; bills of lading and warehouse receipts; certificate of origin or EUR.1 certificates; customs declarations (ENS/EXS in the EU); quality and health certificates per EU food-law requirements; insurer cargo certificates; counterparty sanctions screening reports from a reputable sanctions-screening provider

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Predominance of offshore counterparties or high-risk jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: OECD/EU blacklist clearance of all contracting parties; document-based economic-purpose narrative for each offshore counterparty; full contractual trail from producer to end-buyer; UBO disclosures of all offshore counterparties; sworn statements confirming absence of shell or shelf counterparty arrangements

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Non-resident partners execute a capital call, then remit subscription proceeds via SWIFT MT103 (or instant TARGET2/SEPA credit if EUR) to the SCSp's EUR or USD account at a Luxembourg Tier 1 bank. The SWIFT field 70/remittance information must reference the SCSp name, the capital-call reference, and the words 'SCSp capital contribution — no invoice'. No Luxembourg Ministerial authorisation, BCL foreign-exchange approval, or ECB prior notification is required. For statistical purposes, the receiving Luxembourg bank reports the flow to the BCL under the balance-of-payments code for direct investment equity capital (category 'Direkte Kapitalanlage / Equity Capital') when the threshold is met; the compliance file should retain the signed capital call, the contributing partner's board resolution or partnership resolution, the remittance receipt (MT103 confirmation), and the bank's foreign-transaction taxation/AML verification records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails are (i) SWIFT MT103/TT wire transfers for open-account settlements to dairy suppliers and logistics providers; (ii) commercial documentary letters of credit issued by the Luxembourg bank via SWIFT MT700, with amendments via MT707 and negotiation settlements via MT740/MT752; and (iii) TARGET2/SEPA euro payments for intra-EEA settlements. USD milk powder trade is settled via SWIFT in cleared USD or through a correspondent USD account; outbound disbursements must cite the relevant trade-invoice and conform to the bank's customer due-diligence refresh procedures. All outbound wire instructions require the transaction-purpose description, counterparty VAT/TAXIN identification where applicable, and screening against EU restrictive-measures lists.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD FX forward contracts (non-deliverable or deliverable, up to 12-month tenor)
EUR/USD FX options and collars (plain vanilla calls, puts, and zero-premium structures)
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD floating-to-floating or fixed-to-floating swaps)
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on offshore CNY (CNH) and other restricted emerging-market currencies
FX swaps (swap against tomorrow) for short-dated working-capital matching

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of beneficial owners (UBO) – RBE confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) maintained by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR); electronic submission via MyGuichet.lu
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15 April through 15 June of each calendar year; any change in beneficial ownership must additionally be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or omitted confirmation may expose the SCSp and its general partners to an administrative fine up to EUR 10,000; deliberate or repeated non-compliance is a criminal offence subject to a fine up to EUR 250,000 and/or imprisonment up to 5 years and publication of the breach on the RBE register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory audit solely by virtue of SCSp status. A statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) becomes compulsory when the SCSp exceeds, at two consecutive financial year-ends, at least two of: balance sheet total > EUR 4,400,000; net turnover > EUR 8,800,000; average employees > 50. If the SCSp is operated under CSSF supervision (e.g., as an AIF or CIV), the CSSF may impose an audit irrespective of size.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP in accordance with the Law of 19 December 2002 on commercial accounts and the Luxembourg Plan Comptable Normalisé; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for consolidated financial statements and may be voluntarily adopted.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year the SCSp must authenticate and confirm its UBO data in the electronic RBE register during the statutory window. For a transfer of partnership interests, an update must be submitted within 30 days; the subsequent annual confirmation must reflect the post-transfer ownership chain. The general partner is responsible for the accuracy of the confirmation and for providing underlying documentation to the registered agent.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Limited Partners and General Partners)
Register of Directors / General Partner Resolutions
Minute Book (Partnership Meetings and Written Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 0 if audit-exempt; voluntary or large-entity audit typically USD 8,000 – 22,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City combined effective rate for a fully taxable corporate partner: 17% national CIT + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax; the national CIT headline rate is 17% above EUR 200,000 taxable income and 15% below EUR 175,000
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: 0% at SCSp level: the SCSp is fiscally transparent and is not itself subject to Luxembourg CIT; profits are allocated to partners and taxed only at partner level. CIT-liable corporate partners may benefit from: (i) 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains; (ii) IP box regime exempting 80% of qualifying IP income, resulting in an effective rate of approximately 5.0%; (iii) notional interest deduction on new equity; (iv) group relief under Luxembourg fiscal unity rules; (v) no net wealth tax for the transparent partnership itself and no capital duty
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for corporate partners (no statutory year cap under Article 114 LIR, subject to the anti-loss-trading rule of Article 114 quinquies LIR); the SCSp itself does not carry losses because income and losses are allocated to partners each tax year
